To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the interfacial MgAl2O 4 formation in the ASZ short‐fiber reinforced AC8A Al‐Mg‐Cu alloy composite is beneficial to the composite strength.
interfacial reaction between the SiO 2 binder layer and the Mg matrix was observed to form MgAl 2 O 4 at the interface, resulting in the improvement of interfacial bonding.
the interfacial reactions between ASZ fibres and AC8A alloy matrix were observed to form MgAl 2O 4 at the interface, which was believed to enhance interfacial bonding.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of interfacial reactions on the mechanical properties in the ASZ short fibrous composite.
the effect of the interfacial reactions on the mechanical properties and the microstructures of the composite.
the effect of the interfacial reactions between the SiO 2 binder layer and the matrix on the mechanical properties, microstructure and microhardness of the short‐fiber‐reinforced AC8A Al alloys.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interfacial bond strength in the composite is not only dependent on the interfacial reactions but also on the amount of Mg in the composite.
the composite containing 1.5% Mg in the matrix exhibited a maximum composite strength of 300 MPa, which is 2.3 times higher than that of the unreinforced AC8A alloy.

the interfacial reactions between the SiO 2 binder layer and the Al alloy matrix were found to be responsible for the improved mechanical properties of the composites, but at the same time, the interfacional reactions were also found to be responsible in the degradation of mechanical properties of the short fibre reinforced Al alloy composites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the interfacial reactions in the AC8A composite are inevitable.
the interfacial MgAl2O 4 reaction was a beneficial process for the ASZ/Al composite.
the composite strength can be improved by interfacial reaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interfacial reactions can be beneficial to the mechanical properties of metal matrix composites if the interfacial layer is designed to be a reaction product of the matrix and fibre.
the Mg content within the composite should be maintained above 2.5 wt% to avoid interfacial reaction.
interfacial reaction is an effective way of enhancing the mechanical properties of short fibre reinforced metal matrix composites.
